control_scope: The finite projector uses distinct conjugate-prime labels above 7 and explicit norm endpoints. The norm-fibre and profile checks are arithmetic controls, not an actual row-family table or a proof of the Mertens bound.
review: The retained strict live cutoff bounds force bounded h,e0,e1 and Ng_l Ng_s asymptotic to D/(E T). The deterministic longer-factor index gives the claimed G lower bound. Original tests are intersections of exact norm intervals after freezing ell_g and its split.

The squarefree row mask on g_l may be removed by the exact q projector, with the original forbidden union imposed on q and the residual b. The cancellation of two Mobius signs requires and retains (q,b)=1. No (g,bar ell) mask is introduced.

The small-q deleted Mertens bound is valid on the whole dyadic interval because G/Nq is at least of order D^(5/64). The deletion radical stays polynomial, and the weighted partial summation preserves endpoints.

No D^epsilon enters the equality norm: tau(ell_g)^2 is the four-factor ideal divisor count on squarefree ell_g, the primitive rational labels are injective, integer norm fibres are dominated by the hyperbola expansion, and the retained tau(d) is explicit. The dual ordinary sieve costs A1 log(2D)+sqrt(A1) T^2.

The large-q row count uses only the good q-part outside the bounded v2 dividing v1. The summed q factor D^(-3/32) is at most T^(-1/2) D^(-1/32) in the stated band. It is absorbed into the subpower gain.

The partner's inherited positive energy still carries D^epsilon and uses its full frequency, including compensation. Pairing gives the stated subpower threshold refinement. It does not produce a new fixed power at e=1/4 and T comparable to one, where the upper comparison still has exponent 13/16.
